nodes.title: Introduction
nodes.description:
This Contractor’s Statement of Work (SOW) defines work to be performed by the Contractor under the contractual authority of the OGM Customer Contractor, Airbus Defence and Space.

The OGM Implementation Phase will be conducted in three major phases:

- Phase B2: Preliminary Definition

- Phase C/D: Detailed Definition and Qualification/Acceptance

- Phase E: Utilisation

- Phase F: Disposal

This Statement of Work (SOW) is applicable in conjunction with the _Generic SOW (GSOW) [AD-02],_ which defines the equipment generic requirements. In case of conflict, this specific statement of work shall have precedence.

nodes.title: Scope of the Document
nodes.description:
The equipment subject of this Statement of Work (SOW) is the DC harness (hereinafter referred to only as “harness”) for the OGM Project, which is defined by the Harness Requirements Specification [AD-03]. This Harness SOW defines the tasks of the harness supplier for:

- The design, development, qualification, manufacturing, integration, test and delivery of the equipment,

- The provision of tooling, test and support equipment, support services and transportation services to support instrument and spacecraft assembly, integration, test and launch, associated with the harness operation and handling.

- The preparation and delivery of documentation.

In addition, tasks and deliverables are categorized into baseline tasks and optional tasks. Both kinds of tasks may occur in this SOW. Unless not specifically identified to the contrary, all task and deliverables specified hereafter shall belong to the baseline tasks. Options are collected at §4.4 Options.

The requirements of this SSOW shall also be made applicable to the contractually specified Lower Level Subcontractors/Suppliers, as pertinent to their work shares. Therefore the word "Supplier" shall be interpreted as “Supplier and Lower Level Subcontractors/Suppliers”, if not specifically restricted. Hardware from other sources, such as OTS items, shall be procured according to the equivalent technical, quality and safety related requirements.

nodes.title: Documents
nodes.description:
The work carried out by the Contractor and possibly its lower-level Subcontractors shall be performed in accordance with the following applicable documents which form an integral part of the Contractor’s SOW. Unless a specific issue of a document is mentioned, the current issue shall apply. When a specific issue is referenced, only that issue applies.

In case technological limitations lead to non-compliances these non-compliances shall be justified and identified as risks by the Contractor for assessment on system level by the Customer. To support this assessment the Contractor shall define the best achievable value/ solution.

The Contractor is requested to issue a Statement of Compliance according to [AD-00] CADL (OGM-LIADSO-21001108453) with the following meaning:

- “D” means Detailed SoC, i.e. for each requirement inside the document,

- “G” means General SoC, i.e. at document level,

- “AM” means SoC for each requirement, which is applicable through the corresponding Applicability Matrix.

In case of evolution, the new issues will be subject to the change process and listed in addition to the SSOW, if not up to date, or the SSOW updated in each specific procurement contract.

nodes.title: Terms and Definitions
nodes.description:
The use of “shall”, “should”, “must”, “will”, “may” and “could”:

- The word “shall” in the text denotes a mandatory requirement. Deviation from such a requirement is not permissible without the formal agreement of Airbus Defence and Space.

- The word “should” in the text denotes a recommendation or advice on implementing a requirement. Such recommendation or advice is expected to be followed unless good reasons are stated for not doing so.

- The words “must” or “will” in the text denotes a provision, a service or an intention in connection with a requirement.

- The words “may” or “could” in the text denote a permissible practice or action and do not express a requirement.

nodes.description: The requirements hereinafter are applicable to the activities of the Supplier and its lower tier SubCos.

nodes.title: Subcontractor responsibilities
nodes.description:
The Supplier shall be responsible for:

1. Detailed engineering of the harness.

2. Definition of the harness detailed design for manufacturing (Manufacturing Design)

3. Parts procurement for harness manufacturing and integration, incl. restrain system.

4. Manufacturing of the harness and all its subassemblies.

5. Option 2: Integration of the harness and all its subassemblies (refer to section 4.4)

nodes.title: Changes until PDR
nodes.description:
Neither the detailing nor the adaptation of the design until PDR shall cause Class A contract change by the Supplier or any of its lower tier SubCos, unless related to material or manufacturing workload costs.

Phase B2, from Kick-Off until PDR, is envisaged as continuous co-engineering activity. Additional related clause is in §4.5 Schedule, HAR SSOW-54 / Co-engineering .

nodes.title: Detail engineering responsibility
nodes.description:
The Supplier shall be responsible for the detail engineering of the harness.

The detail engineering shall consist on:

- _Electrical detail design for manufacturing and integration of the harness.

- _Mechanical detail design of the harness and all mechanical elements of the restrain system.

- _All necessary analysis to perform theoretical or empirical evaluations

nodes.title: Inconsistencies and improvement
nodes.description: The Supplier shall point out all non-compliances, inconsistencies and all unfeasibility items found out in the specification and CAD/ICDs provided by the Prime/Customer, and propose feasible solutions and solutions for improvement, to be discussed and agreed with the Prime/Customer.

nodes.title: Electrical detail design
nodes.description:
The Prime/Customer shall provide the Supplier with a harness EICD containing:

- _Signal types, defining all type of interfaces and cable used.

- _Unit list, units with interfaces to be connected

- _Harness connector list, defined all connector types as generic P/N, eg. DAMA 15S.

- _Signal list, containing all signals wired in the EICD

- _For non-dissipative lines and lines not subject of Vd and resistance analysis, the gauge is also defined in the Pin2Pin, eg. TP24

- _Dissipative lines and lines subject of Vd and resistance analysis, the gauge is either not defined, eg. TPxx, or provisionally defined but to be confirmed with the analysis.

The Supplier shall then be responsible for the electrical detail design of the harness for manufacturing and integration.

The electrical detail design shall consist on:

- _Harness connector list, with P/N selection for all connectors including backshells, screwlocks screengrills and any other accessory.

- _Wiring Diagrams, introducing all necessary modifications for manufacturing and integration of the harness, eg. all splices, whilst fulfilling the electrical connectivity defined by the Prime/Customer.

- _Wiring list (aka. Manufacturing LinkList) comprising the manufacturing configuration of the harness, with P/N’s and all modifications introduced in the schematics for manufacturing and integration of the harness.

- _P/N selection of all cable types and unique identification for each cable in the harness.

- _Bundle/branch definition (bundle naming, etc) for each cable, including all segregation information, that is EMC, Main/Red, TCS/Crimp-AIT.

- _P/N selection of all electrical parts of the HW eg, splices, terminals, etc.

nodes.title: Computer media for exchanging electrical design
nodes.description:
The Prime/Customer shall provide the Supplier with a harness EICD in electronic Excel file.

The Supplier shall provide on a computer media, in Excel or Access.

nodes.title: Mechanical detail design
nodes.description:
The routing boundary conditions (stay-out areas, preliminary path definition and integration sequence) of the harness are to be primarily defined by the Prime/Customer. Prime/Customer will provide the Supplier with the routing boundary conditions and shall then be revisited together with the harness Supplier for feasibility and improvement in mutual agreement.

The Supplier shall be responsible for the mechanical detail design of the harness for manufacturing and integration.

The mechanical detail design shall consist on:

- _Detailed routing design in CATIA of the bundles defined in the electrical detail design.

- _Definition and location of all harness fixation points.

- _Definition of all harness connector brackets and all its support secondary-structures in CATIA incl. stress analysis of the restrain system components. (input to prime/customer as need for inserts on the structural panels)

- _Definition of all mechanical drawings (harness layout, fixation points location with items identification and location)

- _Definition of the manufacturing mockup.

- _P/N selection of all mechanical parts and materials of the HW (eg.backshells and its accessories, screw locks and jackposts, tie-raps, foils, tapes, sleeves, etc.).

nodes.title: Routing drawings
nodes.description:
The supplier shall be responsible for the definition of all routing drawings and associated part lists:

- _Showing the configuration of the harness routing as it is on-board and on the representative manufacturing mockup

- _Identifying the different bundles according to Main/Redundant lines, EMC class and thermal control segregation.

- _Uniquely identifying each fixation attachment point –tie-base, stand off, etc-.

- _Temporary attachments, if any, for proper transfer of the harness onto the structure.

nodes.title: CAD models
nodes.description:
The harness Supplier shall implement in the CAD model of the S/C, which is provided by the Prime/Customer, the complete CAD model of the real harness, comprising

- _all bundles incl. routing up to each thermal control item.

- _connectors with backshell and any mounting accessory,

 _attachment points (eg. tie-bases, stand-offs)

- _all connector brackets

and return the harness CAD model in regular stages to the Prime/Customer. The Supplier shall envisage this activity as an iterative process, especially until PDR. The data file format is CATIA 3DExperience 2018x (tbc)

nodes.title: Design ä analysis
nodes.description:
The Supplier shall be responsible for all necessary analysis to perform theoretical or empirical evaluations, in particular following major analysis:

- _FMCA (A)

- _Reliability (A)

- _WCA (A)

- _mass budget (A)

- _Option 3: voltage drop, current derating and thermal dissipation analysis (B) (refer to section 4.4)

- _Option 4: thermal analysis of the bundle (overshielded bundles) (A) (refer to section 4.4)

- _strength/stress analysis of the restrain system components, etc (A)

Analysis categorized (A) shall be provided for the respective reviews.

Analysis categorized (B) shall be provided for the respective reviews and as requested by the Customer to iterate on the latest HW implementation.

nodes.title: Approval of the manufacturing processes
nodes.description:
The selection of all manufacturing procedures, crimp interconnections and combinations (eg. splice, terminals) shall be submitted to Prime Contractor approval.

Manufacturing procedures shall be reviewed by Prime/Customer at Supplier site.

Crimping shall be carried out in accordance with ECSS-Q-ST-70-26C , ‘Crimping of High Reliability Electrical Connections’.

Soldering shall be carried out in accordance with ECSS-Q-ST-70-08C , ‘Manual Soldering of High Reliability Electrical Connections’.

All manufacturing personnel shall be certified to the above mentioned specifications.

New manufacturing methods / processes shall be investigated and verified on sample basis, the implementation on FM hardware shall be performed after authorization by the customer.

nodes.title: Cleanliness and Contamination Control Plan (CccP)
nodes.description: A Cleanliness & Contamination Control (CCCP) plan shall be established by the harness supplier. Main results of the harness contamination analysis (outgassing) shall be included. Consideration shall be given to cleanability as a design feature of parts, i.e. the possibility of accidental contamination shall be taken into account.

nodes.title: Harness cleaning procedure
nodes.description: Harness cleaning procedure shall be established by the harness supplier. Dedicated section shall be included to describe how cleaning could be performed in case of accidental contamination

nodes.title: Integration activities
nodes.description:
All Harness hardware installed on instrument/satellite structures by the harness Contractor at customer facilities shall be witnessed and monitored by harness Contractor authorized QA. Any harness integration work shall be documented in procedures, as-runs and reports by the harness supplier and provided to the Customer. Inspections shall be identified (MIP), as a minimum.

- _Prior to integration onto the FM structure, the harness shall have successfully passed the manufacturing tests and the bake-out.

- _After any harness / wiring installation, the interconnections shall pass an isolation, continuity & resistance test and inspections documented in the integration procedure.

- _All crimped items interconnected during integration shall be successfully tested in isolation, continuity and resistance. The results shall be recorded and submitted to the customer.

The Supplier shall be responsible for the integration of the harness at Customer premises, incl.:

- _installation of the harness bundles at Prime/Customer premises,PL IOM harness in ISO5 and the PF IEM harness in ISO8, both in Ottobrunn,,

- _connection of all harness flying leads as part of the harness integration activities (mostly thermal control)

- _electrical integration tests as part of the harness integration activities, incl. Grounding, Isolation, Continuity and Resistance measurements, before and after connection of the item.

nodes.title: Integration and post-integration documents
nodes.description: The Supplier shall establish all documents for integration of the harness and post integration maintenance by the Prime/Customer, incl. integration and test procedures, handling, maintenance, repairing, cleaning and storage procedures.

nodes.title: Final routing inspection report after integration

The contractor shall perform and issue to the customer, a photo documentation of all bundles integrated on FM structures fixed to the anchor attachment and the interconnection of the crimped end-items.

nodes.title: Mass measurement
nodes.description:
Mass of bundles:

On completion of the manufacturing, the assemblies shall be weighed and this figure reported in the Mass Report at PTR.

Mass added during AIT:

The integration procedure shall reflect the measurement of all masses not weighed so far but introduced during AIT ("kit mass") as follows:

1. Measure complete kit mass before integration.

2. Integrate kit parts.

3. Weigh surplus masses not integrated (like cut part of tie-raps, cut flying leads, etc).

4. The integrated mass is to be obtained by difference between complete kit mass minus surplus kit mass.

The integrated mass shall be reported in the updated Mass Report for final DRB.

Mass of restrain system components:

The tie-bases, cable ties, harness supports, connector brackets and any other on-board ancillary part shall be weighed separately and the total reported in the Mass Reports.

This mass of the brackets shall be reported in the Mass Report at PTR. The mass of the elements integrated (tie-bases and tie-raps, protective foil) shall be reported in the Mass Report for final DRB)
